meta.title: Proposition 123 rental income and rent rules
meta.review_reason: DOLA must issue guidance on renting units in its home ownership program by 2026-12-31 (SB26-040), and the AHFF guidelines are revised each fiscal year.
meta.scope: Income and rent limits for rental housing funded by Colorado Proposition 123 (C.R.S. Title 29, Article 32), by program, plus the rule DOLA uses to count rental units toward local commitments.
meta.methodology: Every limit is copied from the statute or the current program guidelines and carries a verbatim quote. A rule that could not be confirmed from a primary source is null with a reason. The only computed part is rent_table_deviations, which compares CHFA's published maximum rents with the 30% rule.
meta.rent_formula: Where the rule is a gross rent of 30% of the unit's income limit, CHFA's published maximum rents apply it as 30% of the income limit for 1.5 persons per bedroom (one person for a studio), divided by 12 and rounded down.
meta.not_included: For-sale and down-payment programs, homelessness rental assistance and vouchers, and local inclusionary rules.

programs.name: Affordable Housing Equity Program
programs.fund: Affordable Housing Financing Fund (OEDIT; CHFA is contract administrator)

income_rule.per_unit_max_reason: Neither the statute nor the guidelines set a per-unit maximum; the FAQ says individual units may be above or below 90% AMI as long as the average holds.

rent_rule.rule: Gross rent may not exceed 30% of the income limit designated for the unit.
rent_rule.utility_allowance: CHFA Specialized Multifamily Loan Programs Utility Allowance Policy (G8), unless the regulatory agreement says otherwise.
rent_rule.annual_increase_cap_reason: No annual rent-increase cap appears in the statute or any guideline read. G8 allows increases only at lease renewal; the 3% figures in the guidelines are underwriting discounts to market rent, not increase caps.
rent_rule.underwriting: Rents underwritten at least 3% below local market rents (G1).

programs.ami_source: HUD area median income as published by HUD or a statewide housing authority (CHFA)

evidence.claim: Project average of designated income at or below 90% AMI; gross rent at most 30% of the unit's income limit
evidence.quote: average designated imputed income by household size for projects funded by the program must not exceed 90% of the area median income as established by the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development and published by the department or a statewide political subdivision or authority on housing, and regulated units in the project must have a gross rent limit that does not exceed thirty percent of the imputed income limitation applicable to the units

evidence.claim: 90% is an average across restricted units
evidence.quote: Not to exceed 90% average AMI for all restricted units

evidence.claim: No per-unit cap
evidence.quote: Individual units may be more or less than 90 percent AMI

evidence.claim: 30-year affordability
evidence.quote: A Regulatory Agreement ensuring affordability for 30 years will be required

evidence.claim: Rent increases only at renewal
evidence.quote: Mid-term rent increases prohibited

programs.name: Concessionary Debt Program: Multifamily Finance (low- and middle-income rental and preservation)
programs.fund: Affordable Housing Financing Fund (OEDIT; CHFA is contract administrator)

income_rule.per_unit_max_reason: No per-unit maximum is stated. Up to 25% of units may be unrestricted but are excluded from the financing (G3). If the Prop 123 loan is subordinate, the senior lender's AMI rules may govern instead.

rent_rule.rule: Gross rent may not exceed 30% of the income limit designated for the unit.
rent_rule.utility_allowance: CHFA Specialized Multifamily Loan Programs Utility Allowance Policy (G8), unless the regulatory agreement says otherwise.
rent_rule.annual_increase_cap_reason: No annual rent-increase cap appears in the statute or any guideline read. G8 allows increases only at lease renewal; the 3% figures in the guidelines are underwriting discounts to market rent, not increase caps.
rent_rule.underwriting: Rents underwritten at least 3% below local market rents (G3).

programs.ami_source: HUD area median income as published by HUD or a statewide housing authority (CHFA)
programs.affordability_basis: guideline: the greater of the loan term or 30 years

evidence.claim: Project average at or below 60% AMI; gross rent at most 30% of the unit's income limit
evidence.quote: SUBPROGRAMS SPECIFIED IN SUBSECTIONS (1)(c)(I), (1)(c)(II), AND (1)(c)(III) OF THIS SECTION MUST NOT EXCEED 60% OF THE AREA MEDIAN INCOME

programs.fund: Affordable Housing Financing Fund (OEDIT; CHFA is contract administrator)

rent_rule.underwriting: Rents underwritten at least 3% below local market rents (G4).

programs.name: Land Banking Program
programs.fund: Affordable Housing Financing Fund (OEDIT; CHFA is contract administrator)

income_rule.predominant_use_note: At least 70% of the project's improved square footage or units must be affordable; the rest may be market-rate, restricted above 60% AMI, or commercial. Projects at 51-69% may apply with a justification (G6).

rent_rule.rule: Gross rent may not exceed 30% of the income limit designated for the unit.
rent_rule.utility_allowance_reason: The Land Banking guidelines name no utility allowance policy, and G8 covers only Equity and Concessionary Debt, so none is confirmed.
rent_rule.annual_increase_cap_reason: No annual rent-increase cap appears in the statute or any guideline read. The 3% figures in the guidelines are underwriting discounts to market rent, not increase caps.

programs.ami_source: HUD area median income as published by HUD or a statewide housing authority
programs.affordability_basis: guideline: at least 30 years after the final improvements; a waiver to 20 years is possible with a market analysis

evidence.claim: Each rental unit at or below 60% AMI; gross rent at most 30% of its income limit
evidence.quote: rental housing that has a designated imputed income limit by household size not to exceed sixty percent of the area median income

evidence.claim: All rental units at or below 60% AMI
evidence.quote: All rental units to be developed on the subject property will be restricted to households with annual incomes at or below 60 percent of the Area Median Income

evidence.claim: Affordability period
evidence.quote: at least 30 years after the final improvements are developed

programs.name: Program serving persons experiencing homelessness (supportive housing development)
programs.fund: Affordable Housing Support Fund (DOLA Division of Housing)

income_rule.max_ami_reason: The statute sets no income limit for this program, and no Prop 123-specific limit was found in DOLA's program page or the combined 2025-2026 supportive housing RFA, which targets extremely low-income households alongside vouchers.

rent_rule.rule: Not confirmed for Prop 123 capital awards.

commitment_counting.cost_rule: Costs the household less than 30% of its monthly income.
commitment_counting.rent_basis_note: For counting units toward a local commitment, DOLA counts the rent payment only and excludes utilities (D1). This differs from the gross-rent limit the OEDIT programs use.
commitment_counting.averaging_from_2027: A project with a deed restriction of at least 15 years whose average rent is affordable at or below 60% AMI counts every unit (C.R.S. 29-32-105(3)(d)(I)(E), added by HB26-1313).
commitment_counting.deep_affordability_bonus: From 2027 a unit restricted at or below 40% AMI counts as 1.2 units (C.R.S. 29-32-105(9)(d)).

evidence.claim: Rental affordable housing is at or below 60% AMI and costs less than 30% of income
evidence.quote: "Affordable housing" means rental housing affordable to a household with an annual income of at or below sixty percent of the area median income, and that costs the household less than thirty percent of its monthly income.

evidence.claim: Utilities excluded when counting
evidence.quote: For rental, the housing costs include the rental payment. Excluded from the housing costs are utility payments of any kind.

evidence.claim: Averaging allowed from 2027
evidence.quote: Rental projects that are subject to a 15-year minimum deed restriction, may use income averaging at 60% AMI.

rural_resort_petitions.rule: A rural resort community may petition DOLA to use different AMI percentages for Land Banking, Equity and Concessionary Debt (C.R.S. 29-32-105.5(3)); an approved petition holds for the current three-year cycle.
rural_resort_petitions.note: AMI percentages are the levels DOLA lists for each petition. Where DOLA lists one percentage without splitting rental and ownership, it is recorded for both. Only approved petitions change a program limit.

conflicts.detail: The OEDIT programs limit gross rent (rent plus CHFA utility allowance and required fees). DOLA's commitment counting uses the rent payment only and excludes utilities.

The Land Banking guidelines restrict all rental units to 60% AMI. DOLA's petition page says units may exceed the limit if the development averages at or below it. This file follows the guidelines, which govern awards.
The Equity guidelines still say the average of rents must not exceed 90% AMI, the pre-2023 statutory wording. Since HB23-1304 the statute averages designated income, which this file follows.

CHFA's 2026 tables carry Prop 123 rural resort tiers, but no Prop 123 guideline names that table as the governing one, and how HERA and hold-harmless limits apply to Prop 123-only projects is not stated.

The compiled C.R.S. could not be reached. The statutory text here is assembled from the voter-approved text and the enacted session laws, and checked against HB26-1360's plain-text reprint of 29-32-104(1)(a) and (1)(b).

rent_table_deviations.note: Cells in CHFA's 2026 table whose published maximum rent differs from 30% of the income limit for 1.5 persons per bedroom. Each value matches CHFA's PDF as published. For a Prop 123 unit the statutory cap is the 30% rule, so where the published rent is higher it overstates the Prop 123 limit.
